battle.name: 康布雷
battle.theater: 西線法國北部康布雷戰區
battle.brief: 一九一七年十一月二十日，英軍第三軍以數百輛馬克四菱形戰車，在極短的砲擊準備後成縱隊撞開德軍興登堡防線，一日之內向內推進數公里，俘虜近萬。缺口只維持數日：步兵與炮火沒有跟進，德軍預備隊就把防線重新拉直。

kit.name: 馬克 IV
kit.history: 一戰英軍產量最高的菱形戰車。康布雷證明集中使用能撕開防線，也證明沒有步兵與補給時缺口會重新合上。

countries: 康布雷一役由英軍第三軍對德軍第二軍在西線北段康布雷周邊打響，交戰地帶由聖康坦運河向東伸至塞勒河，核心是德軍一九一七年新築的欣登堡防線，其中最外一道是號稱「碎片陣地」的舍本陣線。英方由總參謀長道格拉斯·黑格統一指揮，實際作戰由朱利安·賓率領第三軍負責，旗下第三軍團由賓直接兼管、第四軍團由羅林森中將、第十二軍團由艾倫比中將率領，三個軍團的砲兵則由休·塔利中將統一節制；坦克兵力集中在第一坦克軍的第一坦克旅，由菲利普·約翰森中校以旅長身份指揮，另有第一、第二軍坦克旅在後方待命，步兵主力包括英國第37、41、20、16師，以及澳軍第2、第5、第6師，英方的基本構想是由坦克撞開防線，再由步兵與騎兵擴大突破口。德方由第二軍司令馬克斯·馮·伯恩中將主持防線，第一線由第14師防守運河與舍本陣線，第26、27師等預備隊負責反擊，軍隊隸屬德軍集團軍群司令庫赫勒中將，最高統帥部則以參謀總長魯登道夫為核心，欣登堡防線本身就是德軍在西線重點經營的堡壘體系。
countriesEn: The Second Battle of Cambrai was fought in the northern sector of the Western Front, between the British Third Army and the German Second Army, in the ground around Cambrai in northern France, running broadly from the St Quentin Canal in the east to the Selle river. At the core of the German position lay the Hindenburg Line, newly built in 1917, whose outermost element was the Scherben Stellung, the concrete 'shattered line'. On the British side the overall command lay with Commander-in-Chief Douglas Haig, but the operation itself was run by General Sir Julian Byng's Third Army, with III Corps under Byng himself, IV Corps under General Rawlinson and XII Corps under General Allenby, while the artillery of all three corps was controlled by General Sir Hugh Tully. The armoured force was concentrated in the 1st Tank Brigade of the 1st Tank Corps, commanded by Lieutenant-Colonel Philip Johnson, with the 1st and 2nd Army Tank Brigades held back in reserve. The infantry component included the British 37th, 41st, 20th and 16th Divisions and the Australian 2nd, 5th and 6th Divisions, and the plan was for the tanks to open the way, with infantry and mounted troops exploiting the gap. On the German side the front was held by the Second Army under General Max von Boehn, the 14th Division manning the canal and the Scherben Stellung, with the 26th and 27th Divisions and other reserves available for counter-attack; the sector formed part of Army Group C under General von Kuchler, while the Hindenburg Line itself was the product of the German General Staff and the engineers, with overall influence exercised from the headquarters of Erich Ludendorff.
people: 英方最關鍵的人物是第三軍司令朱利安·賓。他是一個敢於拿戰車去賭一次突破的指揮官，方案由他與幕僚團策劃，坦克的秘密由他把關，為了保密甚至刻意縮減步兵同步推進的規模。英軍最高統帥部對戰車的態度多有保留，黑格本人更信任炮火消耗而非機械突破，因此策劃過程中屢次把坦克的作用限制在輔助位置。前線執行層面的關鍵人物是第一坦克旅旅長菲利普·約翰森中校，由他安排各連出動次序、故障拖救與臨時維修，以及決定戰車集團的行軍速度與縱隊間隔。設計層面要記一功的是華特·戈登·威爾遜與威廉·特里頓，兩人把馬克三改成菱形履帶佈局的馬克四，讓坦克能夠原地轉向、倒行並越過寬壕溝。德方領袖是第二軍司令馬克斯·馮·伯恩中將，防線上的工事由工兵與步兵師級指揮官掌握，缺口出現後的預備隊反擊則由魯登道夫在最高統帥部直接下令。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the British side was General Sir Julian Byng, commander of the Third Army. He was the officer prepared to gamble a breakthrough on the tanks: he and his staff drew up the plan, he guarded the secrecy of the tank movement, and to preserve that secrecy he deliberately cut back the scale of the infantry advance that was to follow. The British high command was far from enthusiastic about the new weapon, and Haig himself trusted artillery attrition more than mechanical breakthrough, so during planning the tanks were repeatedly assigned a supporting rather than a leading role. The key man on the firing line was Lieutenant-Colonel Philip Johnson, commanding the 1st Tank Brigade, who organised the order in which companies went forward, the recovery and field repair of broken-down vehicles, and the speed and spacing of the tank columns. On the design side the credit belongs to Walter Gordon Wilson and William Tritton, who turned the Mark III into the Mark IV with its rhomboid track layout, allowing the tank to pivot on the spot, reverse, and cross wide trenches. The German leader was General Max von Boehn, commander of the Second Army; the works on the front were in the hands of the engineers and divisional commanders, and the counter-attack by the reserves once the gap appeared was ordered from the highest command under Erich Ludendorff.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是一九一七年英軍列裝的菱形戰車馬克四，它在康布雷扮演的角色是開路撞擊，而不是攻堅主砲。馬克四全重約二十八噸，乘員八人，裝甲厚度約八至十毫米，主武裝是置於右前側炮闂的六磅速射砲，每車攜彈約一千五百發，另有四挺三〇三式機槍分置兩側炮闂與車尾，動力為道用牌汽油引擎，最高時速約四至五英里，實戰速度更慢。它靠菱形履帶與前後成角度的轉向輪，可以原地轉向與倒行，越過數米寬的壕溝是它最大的本領。輔助裝備方面，每個步兵營配一輛支援型馬克四，攜帶油料、備件與拖救工具，營部另有三點九吋迫擊砲由馬匹牽引跟進，英軍步兵的標準槍械是李-恩菲爾德步槍，砲兵則是六磅野戰砲與重型攻城砲。德方裝備以七點七釐米野戰砲、八點八釐米高射砲配合機槍巢與混凝土碉堡組成舍本陣線，十一月三十日德軍更投入少量A7V戰車應戰，可用數量約十數輛，那是他們第一次用戰車反擊。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Mark IV, the rhomboid tank the British Army put into service in 1917. At Cambrai its role was the battering ram that opened the way, not the heavy gun that reduced fortifications. The Mark IV weighed roughly twenty-eight tons, carried a crew of eight, and had armour of about eight to ten millimetres. Its main armament was a six-pounder quick-firing gun in the right front sponson, with about fifteen hundred rounds carried on board, plus four .303 machine guns, two in the sponsons and two at the rear. Power came from a Daimler petrol engine, giving a maximum of roughly four to five miles an hour and considerably less in the field. The rhomboid track layout and the angled steering wheels front and rear allowed it to pivot on the spot and to reverse, and crossing trenches several metres wide was its greatest strength. In support, each infantry battalion received a support Mark IV carrying fuel, spares and recovery gear, while battalion headquarters towed 3.9-inch howitzers along; the standard infantry arm was the Lee-Enfield rifle, and the artillery fielded six-pounder field guns and heavy guns. On the German side the defences were built of 7.7 cm field guns and 8.8 cm guns interlocking with machine-gun emplacements and concrete blockhouses in the Scherben Stellung, and on 30 November the Germans committed a small number of A7V tanks, perhaps a dozen or so operational, in the first German tank counter-attack of the war.
tactics: 康布雷的戰術核心是「極短的砲擊準備加密集的戰車縱隊」。十一月二十日清晨四點四十分前後，英軍以短時間的炮擊打頭，隨即放戰車越過前線，四百多輛馬克四分批成縱隊推向前方，每輛之間保持間隔，避免單車被擊中停滯而堵塞後隊。戰車的任務是以車體壓過鐵絲網、越過壕溝、逐段消滅機槍巢，並用六磅砲壓制德軍砲兵與據點，理論上再由步兵跟入佔領，騎兵與摩托化部隊負責擴大突破口。德軍反應極快，前線被突破的消息令預備隊沿鐵路輸送，在數日內湧入缺口。英軍原計劃的支援火力並未如期到位：讓炮火逐步向前推移的跟進射擊沒有落實，步兵也受命限制同步推進，於是突破口缺乏佔領與鞏固。缺口就這樣在四至七日內重新閉合，只靠戰車本身守不住攻下的土地。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of Cambrai was a very short artillery preparation followed by a dense mass of tank columns. At about twenty to five past four in the morning of 20 November the British opened with a brief bombardment and then sent the tanks over the front line. More than four hundred Mark IVs advanced in successive echelons, each vehicle keeping a gap so that a single machine hit could not block the column behind it. The tanks were to crush wire with their hulls, cross the trenches, destroy machine-gun emplacements one by one, and use their six-pounders to silence German guns and strongpoints. In theory the infantry would then walk in to occupy the ground, while cavalry and motorised troops widened the breach. The German reaction was very fast: news of the break sent the reserves moving along the railway, and they poured into the gap within days. The supporting fire the British plan required never arrived in time. The creeping barrage meant to move forward with the advance was not delivered, and the infantry were ordered to hold back their own advance, so the breach was never occupied or consolidated. The gap closed again within four to seven days; the tanks alone could not hold the ground they had taken.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下，各書統計略有出入，引用時宜注明。時間：進攻於一九一七年十一月二十日開始，砲擊準備極短，戰役延續至十二月七日。戰車：分配予首波進攻的馬克四通常記為四百七十六輛，部分統計作四百餘輛，集中於第一坦克軍第一坦克旅；每車乘員八人，載彈約一千五百發六磅砲彈，最高時速約四至五英里。推進距離：部分地段向內推進約八公里，即約五英里。戰果：頭兩日據稱俘虜德軍逾八千人、繳獲火炮上百門，各家數字由八千至一萬不等。傷亡：英軍約四千人至七千人，德軍約兩萬至三萬人（含被俘者），各書估算有出入。防線：舍本陣線前沿約六公里，內有機槍巢五十個以上與數十座混凝土碉堡；跨越聖康坦運河靠工兵架起的一座浮橋，是當時唯一過河通道。反擊時序：德軍於十一月二十三日開始反擊，至三十日前線大致回復原狀。產能方面，馬克四是英軍產量最高的戰車，一九一七至一九一八年間生產超過一千三百輛，常見統計約一千三百七十餘輛。
dataEn: The figures that can be stated with a reasonable basis are roughly as follows; the figures differ slightly from book to book and should be quoted with that caveat attached. Dates: the attack opened on 20 November 1917 after a very short artillery preparation, and the battle ran on to 7 December. Tanks: the Mark IVs allocated to the first wave of attack are usually given as four hundred and seventy-six, with some counts putting it at rather more than four hundred, concentrated in the 1st Tank Brigade of the 1st Tank Corps; each vehicle had a crew of eight and carried about fifteen hundred rounds of six-pounder ammunition, with a maximum speed of roughly four to five miles an hour. Depth of advance: in places the front was pushed about eight kilometres, that is about five miles, inward. Results: the first two days are said to have yielded more than eight thousand German prisoners and over a hundred captured guns, estimates ranging from eight thousand to ten thousand. Casualties: British losses of about four to seven thousand, German losses of about twenty to thirty thousand including prisoners, with wide variation between the estimates. The defences: the Scherben Stellung ran for about six kilometres of front, containing more than fifty machine-gun emplacements and several dozen concrete blockhouses, and the only crossing of the St Quentin Canal was a single pontoon bridge built by the engineers. The timing of the counter-attack: the Germans counter-attacked from 23 November, and by the 30th the front had been substantially restored. On production, the Mark IV was the most numerous British tank of the war, with more than thirteen hundred built between 1917 and 1918, a commonly quoted figure being around thirteen hundred and seventy.
cause: 康布雷不是突然決定的一場戰役，而是一九一七年西線長期消耗之後，英軍企圖用一次攻勢打破僵局的產物。前一年的索姆河與凡爾登兩場消耗戰，加上同年海牙的三次戰役，令英軍步兵實力耗盡，連續的定量攻勢失敗，士氣低落；與此同時德軍把一九一七年的主要兵力和工程力量集中到興登堡防線，西線陷入所謂的地塹僵局。英軍高層認為傳統步兵攻勢難以奏效，於是押注新裝備：馬克四自一九一七年年初開始秘密生產與交付，數量雖然有限，但已足以編成一個完整的坦克旅。賓的方案刻意保密，希望用戰車作突擊手段打亂德軍部署；德軍因情報失誤，多以為英軍只會重演炮擊加步兵衝鋒的舊套路，結果在幾個小時內被連續突破。第二個誘因是康布雷一帶屬北法重要的煤礦區與交通樞紐，英方希望用一次成功突破扭轉士氣與資源分配。而德軍集團軍群抽調資源應付意大利戰線，也令其在西線感到壓力。
causeEn: Cambrai was not a sudden decision. It was the product of an attempt by the British to break the deadlock of the Western Front after a year of attrition in 1917. The battles of the Somme and Verdun the previous year, followed by the three battles of Ypres in the same year, had exhausted British infantry, and one quantitative attack after another had failed while morale sagged; at the same time the Germans concentrated their troops and engineering effort on the Hindenburg Line, and the Western Front settled into what was called a trench stalemate. The British high command concluded that a traditional infantry attack could not succeed, and so staked its credit on new equipment: the Mark IV had been in secret production and delivery since the beginning of 1917, and although the numbers were limited they were enough to form a complete tank brigade. Byng's plan was deliberately kept secret in the hope that tanks would strike as a surprise and disrupt German dispositions. German intelligence was wrong, and the enemy expected little more than the familiar bombardment followed by an infantry push, only to be broken through several times over within a few hours. A second inducement was that the Cambrai area was an important coal-mining district and transport hub of northern France, and the British hoped a successful breakthrough would reverse both morale and the allocation of resources. The German army group was also drawing resources away to meet the situation in Italy, which added pressure on its western front.
impact: 康布雷是裝甲戰術的分水嶺。它第一次把數百輛戰車集中在一條數公里的正面，直接在德軍防線上撕開缺口，而且代價極低：步兵未付出重大傷亡，突破的深度也遠超此前任何一次攻勢，令「機械化可以取代步兵攻堅」這個命題第一次得到實戰證明，雖然只是短暫的。但同一場戰役也證明了反命題：如果沒有步兵佔領、沒有炮火支援、沒有足夠補給，缺口就會在數日內重新閉合。這個教訓令英軍在一九一八年把戰車升格為獨立兵種，成立坦克軍，並在春季攻勢中以大量戰車配合同種火力支援再作嘗試；德軍方面亦受刺激加速發展A7V，並在一九一八年提出更完整的合成戰術理論。康布雷同時成為「定點攻勢」學說最重要的實戰樣板：一個策劃完善、保密到家、裝備新穎的攻勢可以成功突破，卻因為戰略目標模糊而無法轉化為勝利。
impactEn: Cambrai was a watershed in armoured warfare. For the first time several hundred tanks were concentrated on a front of only a few kilometres and tore a breach straight through the German defences, and the cost was very low: the infantry paid no heavy toll, and the depth of the penetration was greater than that of any earlier attack. The proposition that mechanisation could take the place of the infantry assault was thus demonstrated in battle for the first time, even if only briefly. The same battle also demonstrated the opposite proposition: without infantry to occupy the ground, without artillery support and without adequate supply, a breach will close again within days. That lesson led the British to raise the tank to an independent arm in 1918, to form tank corps, and to try again with massed tanks supported by massed artillery in the spring offensive. On the German side the shock accelerated the development of the A7V and produced a more complete German theory of combined arms in 1918. Cambrai also became the most important operational model of the set-piece doctrine: an attack that was thoroughly planned, perfectly concealed and equipped with something new could break through, and yet achieved nothing decisive because its strategic aim was never defined.
result: 點算數：康布雷是一場戰術上成功、戰略上無結論的戰役。十一月二十日的突破屬實，英軍越過德軍第一道與第二道陣地，向內推進最深約八公里，頭幾日俘虜近萬人、繳獲大量火炮與軍械；澳軍第5師在北段與第6師在十二月四日的反攻亦收復部分失地，英軍最終保住聖康坦運河以北的部分陣地與若干村莊，戰線重新回到僵持。德軍方面，十一月三十日在聖康坦投入第一批A7V戰車反攻，迫使英軍收縮，並把防線重新拉直；英軍第四、第十二軍團等部則在缺口兩側長期進攻，消耗德軍兵力。戰役最終以雙方重新對峙告終，英軍佔地有限，未能轉成戰略突破，卻證實了一件事：集中使用戰車確實可以撕開防線，而決定缺口能不能維持下去的，從來不是戰車本身，而是跟得上的步兵、跟得上的炮火和跟得上的補給。這個教訓在一九一八年被寫進英軍戰術手冊，成為大戰後期裝甲部隊使用的基本原則。
resultEn: Taking stock of it: Cambrai was a tactical success and a strategic non-result. The breakthrough of 20 November was real. The British crossed the first and second German positions, drove inward as far as about eight kilometres in places, and in the first days took nearly ten thousand prisoners together with large quantities of guns and stores. The Australian 5th Division in the northern sector and the 6th Australian Division in the counter-attack of 4 December recovered some of the lost ground, and the British finally held a portion of the front north of the St Quentin Canal together with a number of villages, and the line returned once more to stalemate. On the German side the first A7V tanks were committed in an attack at St Quentin on 30 November, forcing the British to pull back and straighten the front again, while British corps such as IV and XII kept up the pressure on both flanks of the gap and wore down the German troops. The campaign ended in a renewed stand-off: the British gains were limited and were never converted into a strategic breakthrough, yet the battle proved one thing beyond doubt. Concentrated use of tanks can indeed tear open a defence, and what decides whether the breach holds is never the tanks themselves, but the infantry that keep up with them, the artillery that keeps up with them, and the supply that keeps up with them. That lesson was written into British tactical manuals in 1918 and became the basic principle for the employment of armoured formations in the closing stages of the war.
